meta.title: Quests
meta.description: Every quest in Pokémon Emerald Rogue — main quests, challenges and mon masteries — with plain-language triggers, rewards and Vanilla/EX availability.

prose.heading: A data-driven quest system
prose.text: Every quest is defined in JSON, not code: src/data/rogue/quests.json pulls in 13 of the 14 files in src/data/rogue/quests/ via "includes" (template.json is included by nothing), and each file's top-level "defaults" object supplies shared fields (display group, flags, triggers) that individual quests override per-key. At build time the CustomJson tool (quests_c exporter in tools/Pokabbie/Build/CustomJson/QuestExporter.cpp) compiles all of it into one C table consumed by src/rogue_quest.c. The quest files are byte-identical between the two branches — the Vanilla/EX split is done with "#if defined(ROGUE_EXPANSION)" gates on individual quests and rewards, so 94 quests (plus several extra rewards on shared quests) exist only in EX. Names, descriptions and trigger parameters support %TEMPLATE% placeholders (e.g. every mon mastery is one template entry), and the quest log text keeps the game's {PKMN}/{POKEBLOCK} placeholders for "Pokémon"/"Pokéblock".

prose.heading: The nine display groups
prose.text: The Quest Log groups quests into nine display groups, in this order: Final Quests, Starter Quests, Default Quests, Starter Challenges, Default Challenges, Evil Team Challenges, Region Challenges, Type Challenges and Mon Masteries. Each quest carries a display_group (usually inherited from its file's defaults; a few quests, like the "Final Run" in EX, sit in a different group per version). Only Type Challenges is sorted alphabetically in the in-game UI. Starter Challenges is defined in the source but currently holds no quests.

prose.heading: Main quests, challenges and mon masteries
prose.text: There are three quest classes. Main quests (IS_MAIN_QUEST) are one-shot story objectives — once completed they cannot be repeated. Challenges (IS_CHALLENGE) are repeatable: completing one at a higher difficulty unlocks that tier's additional rewards, and challenges stay hidden ("suppressed") until the challenges feature itself is unlocked. Mon masteries (IS_MON_MASTERY) track a species line automatically and keep progressing in the background even while suppressed. Each quest is ACTIVE_IN_RUN, ACTIVE_IN_HUB or both (ACTIVE_ALWAYS). A quest that is not handed over by another quest's reward is UNLOCKED_BY_DEFAULT (unlocked at new game); the rest chain off a "quest unlock" reward — e.g. "Post Game?" unlocks most of the challenge content.

prose.heading: How triggers, requirements and rewards work
prose.text: A quest completes or fails when a trigger event fires — run start/end, earning a badge, entering the Hall of Fame, catching a Pokémon, using a field item, a map event, a battle event — and the trigger's condition passes. Conditions check the current difficulty, party composition, config settings, Pokédex progress, money and more; each record's "trigger" field summarises them in plain language. Active quests can also carry requirements: the quest silently fails if one stops being met (e.g. a required item runs out or a setting changes). Rewards are difficulty-tiered: a reward marked HARD is only granted once the quest has been completed at Hard difficulty or above, which is why challenges are worth repeating. {PKMN} and {POKEBLOCK} in names/descriptions are the game's text placeholders for "Pokémon" and "Pokéblock".
